prompt: A defect was fixed in version 3 of an app last week. Why can a tester still meet it today on a real user's phone?
hint: How does an app arrive, compared with a page?

choices.text: Because the server still sends the old answers
choices.why: The fix was in the app; the question is which copy of the app runs.

choices.text: Old versions stay installed
choices.why: Right. A page loads the current version on every visit; an installed APK does not.

choices.text: Because the emulator caches apps between runs
choices.why: The user's phone is not an emulator, and the question is about it.

choices.text: Because a fix to an app takes a month to compile
choices.why: Compiling takes minutes; arriving on every phone is what takes long.

prompt: Match each kind of Android test to where its code runs.
hint: The figure of the section.

pairs.right: on the computer's Java runtime, no Android
on the device, inside the app's process
on the computer, driving the device from outside

prompt: A test has to tap Allow on the notification dialog that appears over Tickets. Which kind of test can do it?
hint: Whose window is the dialog?

choices.text: A local test, since it is the fastest
choices.why: A local test has no screen at all, let alone Android's dialog.

choices.text: An instrumented test, since it runs inside the app
choices.why: Inside the app is exactly where the dialog is not: it belongs to Android.

choices.text: An end-to-end test, from outside
choices.why: Right. It sees the screen as a person does, whichever app drew each part.

choices.text: None: permission dialogs cannot be tested
choices.why: Lesson 21 tests them; it needs a test that can cross apps.

prompt: You did lesson 1 in a VirtualBox virtual machine. Why does the course ask you to install Android Studio on your own system instead of in that machine?
hint: What is the emulator?

choices.text: Because Android Studio is only sold for Windows and macOS
choices.why: It is free, and it runs on Linux too.

choices.text: The emulator is a virtual machine and would need nested virtualisation
choices.why: Right, which most laptops do not offer.

choices.text: Because the app cannot reach boxoffice from inside VirtualBox, whatever the network settings
choices.why: Networking can be arranged; virtualisation inside a virtual machine is the wall.

choices.text: Because boxoffice must move
choices.why: boxoffice may stay where it is; the section says so.

prompt: Which of these does a phone of your own on a USB cable give you that an emulator does not?
hint: Think about what lesson 19 says an emulator hides.

choices.text: The real sensors of that model
choices.why: Right: the emulator imitates them.

choices.text: The manufacturer's own changes to Android
choices.why: Right: an emulator runs Google's Android.

choices.text: Any Android version you ask for
choices.why: That is the emulator's strength; a phone runs the version it has.

choices.text: A reset to a clean state in a second
choices.why: An emulator snapshot does that; a phone does not.

prompt: On Windows, where does the course tell you to run adb, emulator and Appium?
hint: Where is the emulator easy to reach from?

choices.text: Inside WSL, like lesson 1's commands
choices.why: An emulator is hard to reach from inside WSL.

choices.text: In PowerShell, on Windows itself, not WSL
choices.why: Right, with Android Studio and Node installed on Windows.

choices.text: Inside the emulator's own shell
choices.why: adb reaches the emulator's shell; it does not run inside it.

choices.text: In a Codespace
choices.why: A codespace cannot run an emulator at all.

prompt: Inside the emulator, what does http://localhost:8080 reach?
hint: Every machine calls itself localhost.

choices.text: boxoffice on your computer
choices.why: That is 10.0.2.2 from inside the emulator.

choices.text: The emulator's own port 8080
choices.why: Right. localhost is always the machine asking.

choices.text: The first device adb lists
choices.why: adb is not involved in the app's requests.

choices.text: Android Studio's built-in server
choices.why: Android Studio runs no server for the app.

prompt: The emulator gives the computer it runs on the fixed address ___, so the app asks for http://that-address:8080.
hint: Four numbers separated by dots.

prompt: Put the steps that create a virtual device in the order the section gives them.
hint: A phone, then the Android it boots.
items: open Device Manager and press Create Virtual Device
choose the API 35 system image for your processor

prompt: Tickets runs on your own phone over USB. What has to change so that it reaches boxoffice?
hint: A phone has no 10.0.2.2.

choices.text: adb reverse tcp:8080 tcp:8080, and baseUrl set to localhost
choices.why: Right. The phone's own port 8080 then leads to the computer's.

choices.text: Nothing; 10.0.2.2 works from any device
choices.why: It is the emulator's address for its computer, and only the emulator's.

choices.text: boxoffice must listen on port 10022
choices.why: The port is not the problem; the address is.

choices.text: The phone must be rooted
choices.why: adb reverse needs only USB debugging.

prompt: Why does Tickets carry a network security file naming 10.0.2.2?
hint: What does boxoffice speak?

choices.text: To make the requests faster
choices.why: It changes what is allowed, not how fast it goes.

choices.text: To give the app permission to use the internet
choices.why: That is the INTERNET permission in the manifest.

choices.text: Android blocks plain HTTP otherwise
choices.why: Right, and boxoffice is plain HTTP.

choices.text: To encrypt the traffic between the app and boxoffice
choices.why: It allows unencrypted traffic to one address; it encrypts nothing.

prompt: Shows.kt formats a price as "R$ %d,%02d" from priceCents / 100 and priceCents % 100. Which defect does that choice avoid?
hint: What would 6500 / 100.0 have to go through?

choices.text: A price shown in dollars instead of reais
choices.why: The currency is the literal R$; any method would print it.

choices.text: A cent lost to floating-point rounding
choices.why: Right. Whole numbers never round; a float can show 64,99 for 6500 cents.

choices.text: A crash on phones set to English
choices.why: %d does not depend on the phone's language.

choices.text: A request to boxoffice for every row
choices.why: Formatting happens on the phone, from data already loaded.

prompt: Where does MainActivity ask boxoffice for the shows?
hint: Android forbids one place.

choices.text: On the main thread, before the screen is drawn
choices.why: Android forbids network calls on the thread that draws the screen.

choices.text: On a background thread
choices.why: Right, and the result is drawn back on the main thread.

choices.text: Inside ShowActivity, when a show is opened
choices.why: ShowActivity receives the show's data from the list; it asks nobody.

choices.text: In the network security file
choices.why: That file says what is allowed; it asks for nothing.

prompt: How many files does section 05 have you save for the app?
hint: Count the blocks introduced with "save it as".

prompt: `emulator -accel-check` prints `KVM requires a CPU that supports vmx or svm`. What does that tell you?
hint: vmx and svm are the processor's virtualisation instructions.

choices.text: The system image is the wrong one for this processor
choices.why: The check runs before any image is chosen.

choices.text: adb is not running
choices.why: adb has nothing to do with whether the emulator can accelerate.

choices.text: No virtualisation reaches the emulator here
choices.why: Right: switched off in the firmware, or absent, as in a virtual machine.

choices.text: Android Studio needs updating
choices.why: No update adds instructions the processor does not expose.

prompt: The app says it could not reach the box office. Put the checks in the order the section gives them.
hint: From the server outwards.
items: look in Logcat for a CLEARTEXT refusal

prompt: Your phone shows up in adb devices as unauthorized. What fixes it?
hint: Who has not said yes yet?

choices.text: Restarting boxoffice
choices.why: boxoffice is not part of the USB connection.

choices.text: Unlocking the phone and accepting its prompt to trust this computer
choices.why: Right. The phone is waiting for you.

choices.text: Running adb as root
choices.why: The refusal is the phone's, not a lack of rights on the computer.

choices.text: Creating a new virtual device
choices.why: A virtual device does not change a physical phone's trust.

prompt: Which handle does the course prefer for finding the Refresh button?
hint: The first row of the table.

choices.text: Its visible text, Refresh
choices.why: Text changes with the copy and with the phone's language.

choices.text: Its position: the first button
choices.why: Position breaks the moment anything moves.

choices.text: Its resource id, refresh
choices.why: Right. It does not change when a word does.

choices.text: Its colour
choices.why: Colour is not a handle any of these tools offers.

prompt: Match each way of finding an element to when it breaks.
hint: The last column of the table.

pairs.right: the copy changes, or the language does

prompt: An icon-only Share button has no id and no content description, and the Appium test cannot find it. How should the tester write it up?
hint: Who else depends on the tree having something to say?

choices.text: As a limitation of Appium, to work around with a position XPath
choices.why: That makes the test fragile and leaves the real defect in place.

choices.text: As an accessibility defect: a screen reader cannot name it either
choices.why: Right. The same line, a content description, fixes both.

choices.text: As a reason to test the button by hand from now on
choices.why: The defect stays; only the test is lost.

choices.text: As nothing, since the button works when tapped
choices.why: Working for a sighted person with a finger is not working for everybody.

prompt: A test finds the banner with withText("Offline") and passes on your emulator, set to English, and fails on a colleague's, set to Portuguese. What is the better test?
hint: Separate the handle from the assertion.

choices.text: Force every emulator to English before the suite
choices.why: That hides the language the app may fail in.

choices.text: Find the banner by its position in the layout
choices.why: Position is the most fragile handle of all.

choices.text: Accept either word with a regular expression
choices.why: It still finds by text; the next language breaks it again.

choices.text: withId(R.id.banner), then check it is shown
choices.why: Right. The id finds it in any language; the assertion says what matters.

prompt: Tickets shows the offline banner on your emulator although boxoffice answers curl on your computer. Logcat has no CLEARTEXT message. What is the likeliest cause?
hint: The server is up and the rule allowed the request. What is left on the list?

choices.text: boxoffice is down
choices.why: curl on the computer just answered.

choices.text: The network security file is missing from the project
choices.why: Then Logcat would carry the CLEARTEXT refusal.

choices.text: baseUrl points somewhere the emulator cannot reach
choices.why: Right. Inside the emulator, localhost is the emulator.

choices.text: The phone needs adb reverse
choices.why: An emulator reaches its computer at 10.0.2.2; reverse is for a phone.
